classification.split: dataset Training/Testing split; validation carved from Training only; image-level split; no patient identifiers
classification.branch: MRI branch of the MRI–SPECT fusion model
warnings: Trained on MRI only: this is the MRI branch of the MRI–SPECT fusion model. The image-level fusion stage is implemented and measured separately (`evaluate_fusion`), but the paired MRI–SPECT data carries no diagnosis labels, so no classifier is trained on fused images. These metrics describe MRI classification, not multimodal fusion.
The modality feature stage is active: region maps come from the trained multi-class segmentation head. That head's held-out foreground Dice is 0.3725, so the region descriptors below are approximate.

The Kaggle brain-MRI classification dataset carries no patient identifiers, so samples can only be grouped by image identity (training groups byte-identical copies together). Scores from this dataset may still be optimistic if the same patient appears under unrelated filenames.

Using the dataset's own Training/Testing split. It is an IMAGE-level split: this dataset ships no patient identifiers, so slices from one patient may appear on both sides and the test score can be optimistic.
Dropped 134 Training images that are byte-identical to a Testing image, so the test score is not inflated by memorised copies. The Testing set itself was not modified.

fusion.method: Laplacian pyramid fusion of MRI with the SPECT luminance; SPECT chrominance carried through unchanged
warnings: This dataset carries no diagnosis labels, so the fusion stage is measured by reference-free fusion quality only. No classification accuracy is claimed for it, and the method's four-class prediction still comes from its trained MRI branch.
The pairs are supplied pre-registered. This stage fuses them; it does not register them, and a misregistered pair would fuse into a misaligned image.
15 cases only (357 slices). These numbers describe this dataset, not MRI–SPECT fusion in general.

Slices were sampled, not taken whole: every 2th slice with at least 64 annotated voxels, plus one in 8 tumour-free slices (15620 annotated, 2895 tumour-free). A model trained on this sees far more tumour than a whole scan contains.
Slices were resampled to 128×128 from 240×240, so fine structure is lost before the network sees it.

Loss is class-weighted cross-entropy plus soft Dice over the foreground classes. Unweighted cross-entropy scored 0.0 Dice on two of the three sub-regions: predicting background everywhere is a good enough minimum when the regions are this small.

Method 2's segmentation head is trained on BraTS MRI because it is the only source of real multi-region masks; the classifier stage may run on SPECT. This cross-modality step is intentional and recorded, not hidden.
